text: Stavros chose these on 2026-11-27 when adding TTS speed and silence options: text_to_speech takes optional speed and reduce_silence parameters, with config defaults default_speed 1.0 and default_reduce_silence false (Soniox's own name, not 'skip_silence'). The plugin does not check the 0.7 to 1.3 speed range or whether the model supports silence reduction; Soniox returns invalid_request. Rejected: trimming silence at the start and end of the clip (Soniox has no option for it, and it would need audio post-processing). Rejected in review: falling back to 1.0/false when the new config keys are missing (Stavrobot writes manifest defaults for newly-added keys on update) and skipping config parsing when the request gives an override (a broken config value should fail loudly).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Rejected options (2026-11-26): the official soniox Python SDK (we need our own deadline and cleanup, plain requests is easier to mock, and the first uv run downloads less within the 30 s limit); a shared module between the two tools (it needs sys.path changes, so about 20 duplicated lines were accepted instead); a base-URL config (region selects both the api and tts-rt hosts); checking file extensions before upload (Soniox detects the format, and Signal attachments can have odd extensions); a client-side 5000-character check (Soniox already returns a clear 400); a watchdog deadline on in-flight requests (live transcription of a 67 s clip took about 2 s).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Stavros chose these defaults on 2026-11-26: default_voice Sebastian, default_language en, language_hints el,en (he sends voice notes that mix Greek and English). The TTS parameter is 'voice', not ElevenLabs' 'voice_id'. Stavros accepted that this breaks drop-in compatibility because Soniox voices are names. text_to_speech also takes an optional 'language' that ElevenLabs does not have: the language field sets the accent for the whole clip, and the assistant knows which language it wrote.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Stavros chose on 2026-11-27, after text_to_speech timed out on long text: keep text_to_speech sync with a budget of about 300 characters, and add an async text_to_speech_long (about 1800 characters, one Soniox request per call, the agent splits longer text). Measurements from Stavros: Soniox TTS generates a bit faster than real time (a ~50 s clip hit the 30 s sync kill); STT runs about 23x real time, so speech_to_text stays sync. Rejected: making text_to_speech async only (every short reply would arrive as a separate message and could not be batched); sync only with a ~300 character limit (long text becomes many short clips); splitting and joining MP3s inside the tool to get clips longer than Soniox's fixed 2 minute cap (too much code, seams in the voice, not needed yet); a length check in code (descriptions only, as before).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
